iut_type: End Product (Koizumi Lighting, multiple lamp models), bulk free derivative registration for approximately 150 product part numbers via SIG-designated Excel import
customer_question: Now that our main registration is finalized, could you walk us through how to register all of our lighting product part numbers (approximately 150) as additional derivative models?
question_variants: Is there a bulk import method for registering many derivative models at once, rather than entering each one individually?
What exactly do we need to fill in on the provided Excel template before following the registration procedure?
actual_issue: The customer needed to register a very large number (around 150) of additional product part numbers as free derivative models under their now-finalized main registration, and wanted a practical method for doing this in bulk rather than one at a time through the standard registration site interface.
plain_english_explanation: The lab provided two items: a step-by-step procedure document (PDF) and a large-scale derivative-model bulk-import Excel template designated by Bluetooth SIG for this purpose. The customer's task was to first populate the Excel template starting from row 3 onward with the information for each model they wanted to add as a derivative. Then, following the procedure document's steps, the customer needed to skip step (3) specifically, and instead -- at the point in the Product Details screen described by the procedure -- use the 'click here to specify location for SIG-designated Excel sheet' control to upload the populated Excel file, before continuing with the procedure document's step (4) onward as normal. This bulk-upload mechanism allows many derivative models to be registered from a single Excel file rather than requiring the registration site's standard one-at-a-time entry flow.
consultant_answer: We've attached the step-by-step procedure document along with the large-scale derivative-model Excel template designated by Bluetooth SIG for bulk registration. First, fill in your derivative models' information starting from row 3 of the Excel sheet. Then follow the procedure document's steps, but skip step (3) -- instead, at the Product Details screen, use the 'click here to specify location for SIG-designated Excel sheet' control to upload your populated Excel file, then continue with step (4) onward as normal.
decision_logic: When a customer needs to register a large number of derivative product models under an already-finalized main registration, use the SIG-designated bulk Excel import mechanism rather than the standard one-at-a-time registration site flow, since the bulk template is specifically designed to handle large-scale derivative additions efficiently.
final_recommendation: When a customer anticipates needing to register many derivative models (tens or hundreds), proactively offer the bulk Excel import procedure rather than letting them default to the standard one-at-a-time registration flow, and be precise about which step in the standard procedure document gets replaced by the bulk-upload action (in this case, skipping step 3 in favor of the Excel-upload control).
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer attempting to register ~150 derivative models one at a time through the standard site flow, unaware of the bulk Excel import option, would spend significantly more time and effort than necessary.
